About the model

Model v3.2 · schedule board Sun Oct 4 7:03 PM CT · history through 2026-10-04 · 59,551 maps fitted · 477 teams · 2,455 players · market fit on 4,809 priced series.

Teams: Power is the one number. The model's own price on the Elo scale: 1500 is the average listed team, every 100 points is about 14 percentage points of map win probability against that average. Market-taught power, team Elo, player Elo, plus-minus and Weng-Lin (behind More columns) are inputs or cross-checks, not second opinions.

Players: Perf is the one number. The box-score composite the map probability is built from (kills, deaths inverted, economy-adjusted damage, KAST, opening kills, multikills per round), each in standard deviations against an average tier-S player over a 100-map half-life. +1.0 is a top-30 player, +1.3 the top 3. Plus-minus (rounds per map above an average player, teammates and opponents controlled) is the team-results check; it cannot separate players who always play together.

Schedule: times Central. Fair = the board's price (50/50 outcome-taught and market-taught; the lower of the two lineup prices when the roster is flagged). Edge = fair minus the price you would pay, in points; eROI = that edge over the price. Kalshi ask figures are after the taker fee; bid+1 figures are for a resting bid one cent above the current bid (no maker fee, fills only if someone sells into it). BET marks a side that meets betting rules v1:

One row per seriesboth teams stacked, the first team on top. Tap a row to open its markets and details; tap a team to open the match in the Matchup tab.

PinnaclePinnacle's devigged chance, when it posts a line
Kalshithe mid of each team's book in cents (bid / ask on hover); ~ = a book wider than 10c
Edgethe model minus Kalshi's mid, in cents, shown on the side the model likes: green from +2, bold from +5; a dot = no reliable mid
BetBET = the bot's rules bet that team, the markets in grey (series, map 1, map 2); NO BET = they would, but the match is on the possible-fixing list; a dollar amount = what we already hold on that team in this series and its maps

Red rows / POSSIBLE FIXINGa team on the possible-match-fixing list plays (config/betting.json exclude_teams): the match stays on the schedule, the bot places no bets on it, and its results are tracked apart
Amber dotthe listed roster is not the five who played last; the team is priced on the lower of its two lineup prices

Audit

Bot fills only, flagged matches out. Realized ROI on this few matches is mostly luck; the closing-line and the quoted-versus-filled tables are the ones to watch.
What do these columns mean?
ROI and its errorprofit over stake on settled fills; the error resamples whole matches, because a match's series and map bets win and lose together
CLVKalshi's price just before the start minus the price we paid, dollar-weighted, in cents; positive = the market moved our way after we bought. Fills whose close is not a real benchmark are left out
Quoted vs filledevery bet the bot had an order on, split by how many dollars filled. If the model's chance holds up on the bets nobody sold us and collapses on the ones that filled in size, the loss comes from who sells to us, not from the ratings
zhow far the win rate sits from what the model said, in standard errors; beyond about 2 either way is hard to call luck
Hours to startwhen the fill happened relative to the listed start; early fills have beaten the close, large late fills have not
Guide

Power · Power: the model's strength for this team on an Elo scale - 1500 = the average listed team, +100 = about a 64% map win chance against it. It comes from everything the model uses (the five's ratings, team and map Elo, the box score) and is the number the prices rest on.

Impact · Impact: the five's impact ratings added up - rounds per map over an average lineup. The model's strongest input. Players who always play together share the results credit.

+/- rds · Plus-minus: the five's plain plus-minus added up - rounds per map their teams win above average with them playing. The strongest of the older inputs.

Team Elo · Team Elo: a results-only rating of the team, moved by every map it plays (1500 = average). The model's team-level input; weaker than the box-based ratings on its own.

Δwk / Δmo · How Power moved over the last 7 / 30 days (vs the snapshots of 2026-09-27 / 2026-08-29). Form and slumps, not a predictor.

Maps 180d · Maps in the last 180 days - the evidence behind the numbers (under 30 is thin).

Last / Next · The team's last map; its next scheduled series and the model's chance in it.

Extra columns · Mkt power = the same strength from the market-taught version of the model (fitted to Pinnacle's closes instead of results); the live fair blends the two 50/50 Maps 365d = maps in the last year. Lineup = the five the strength is priced on: the listed roster when it has five, else the last five who played.

Colours · Power only (the number the prices rest on): green = the top 10% of the teams shown, deeper toward the best; red = the bottom 10%. Ranks are among the rows on screen, so a filter re-shades them.

Rows · tap a team's row for its five with their Impact, +/- rds and Perf; tap the name for the team card.

Guide

Impact · Impact, our rating: rounds per map a player adds over an average one - his box score (adjusted for opponents and tier) corrected by his teams' results. Predicts results better than any public rating; the model prices with it. Players who always play together share the results credit.

+/- rds · Plus-minus: rounds per map his teams win above average with him playing, teammates and opponents accounted for. The strongest of the older stats; Impact builds on it.

Perf · His box score in one number - kills, deaths, damage, KAST, opening kills, multi-kills - vs an average tier-S player (0 = average; a typical tier S starter about +0.5). No team effects: sort by it for the box score alone.

Δwk / Δmo · How Perf moved over the last 7 / 30 days (vs the snapshots of 2026-09-27 / none yet). Form and slumps; not a predictor, so not in the rating.

Maps 365d · Maps in the last year: the evidence behind his numbers (under 30 is thin); experience counts too - a newcomer starts about 1.4 rounds below a 100-map player with the same box score.

Last · His last map; away a year = his box history faded by half.

Extra columns · Career maps = since 2020. KPR / DPR = kills / deaths per round; ADR/econ = damage per round, discounted against poorly equipped enemies; KAST = share of rounds with a kill, an assist, a survival or a traded death; OPK = opening kills minus opening deaths; MK = multi-kill rounds; Clutch = clutches won; Util = utility used. All tier- and opponent-adjusted, in standard deviations (0 = average): what Impact and Perf are made of - deaths and damage weigh most, KAST is the best single stat, Clutch and Util add nothing.

Colours · green = the top 10% of the players shown in that column, deeper toward the best; red = the bottom 10%; DPR reversed. Ranks are among the rows on screen.

* · not on a current roster (team = his last team).

Column guide
Matchesthe day's series, one line each (map markets folded in): time and tier, the teams, the model's and Pinnacle's chances (first team first), BET when the bot's rules bet a side; a finished series shows its score. S/A keeps tier S and A only. Click a row to explore it.
Win chancefor the first team: the board's model fair, Pinnacle devigged (from = its opening line), Kalshi bid / ask and Edge (model minus Kalshi's mid, cents) for the series and each map market; for two teams not on the board, the model's map / Bo3 / Bo5 chance from their Power ratings
Mapspick maps 1-3 (or click a map in the list) to see the map and series chances move: each map's chance is the board's own map price (for a match not on the board, the Power map chance) shifted by the two teams' map Elo offsets (a model component), and 'any' uses the unshifted price, so with no maps set the series chance is the board's; when a team's listed roster differs from the five who played last, Last five / Roster five switches between the board's two prices (it starts on the one behind the first team's fair; each side's fair takes the lower, so in the list above the two can add up to less than 100, marked *); Picked maps move to the top of the list in play order (M1, M2, M3); click one again to take it out. Likely fills each team's most-picked map (not the other's top ban) and the likeliest decider. The list shows each team's win rate and maps played in the last 180 days, and tags each team's most-picked and most-banned map.
Elo, last 6 monthsteam Elo from map results at the end of every week - the model's own team Elo, replayed; the logos mark whose line is whose
Comparisonunder Win chance: Power, the last 10 series, maps won and maps won above the Elo expectation in the last 90 days, the five's impact ratings added up (the better number bold)
Lineupsthe current five: Maps = maps played for this team (everything our data holds, since June 2020; amber under 20 = new to the team), then the stats from left to right in order of how predictive they are, sorted by Impact: Impact (our own rating - rounds per map a player adds, from his opponent-adjusted box score and his teams' results; the model's main input since 3.0), Perf (our box-score composite in standard deviations; a typical tier S player is about +0.5), K/D, the bo3.gg rating (0-10; maps bo3.gg had not rated when we fetched them are left out), ADR and form (last 10 maps vs the 90-day average; ADR and form not on a phone). Shaded like the Players tab: green = top 10% of the top-600 players (deeper toward the best), red = bottom 10%.
Head to headat the bottom: the record in the last 12 months and the last five meetings (month/day/year) with map scores
